pairs.reason: Both claims describe the same 25% tariff effective May 3 targeting safety-critical components. Claim 1 lists specific items (airbags, windshields, mirrors, seat belts) while Claim 2 adds batteries and seats but confirms identical program details.

Claim 1 cites an April 2 effective date for a general 25% tariff on cars. Claim 2 clarifies a staged implementation: April 3 for fully assembled vehicles and May 3 for auto parts, indicating a progression rather than a contradiction.

Claim 1 describes an exemption expiring April 2 for autos/parts from Mexico/Canada. Claim 2 confirms a one-month exemption granted to U.S. automakers, consistent with the timeline and scope described in Claim 1.

Claim 1 details a 25% tariff on automobiles/parts effective April/May. Claim 2 describes a separate 10% global tariff set for February 2026 with specific exemptions for passenger vehicles, representing distinct programs and dates.
Both claims are identical in text, describing the August extension of 50% steel/aluminum tariffs to include specific car parts. They represent the same scope and policy update.
Claim 1 states a March 12 imposition of 25% tariffs on steel and aluminum. Claim 2 confirms the return of the full 25% tariff on steel and a raise to 25% for aluminum starting March 12, 2025.

Claim 1 identifies tariffs on seat belts and airbags. Claim 2 lists a broader set of safety parts including airbags, bumpers, seat belts, glass, mirrors, and lighting, confirming the inclusion of items mentioned in Claim 1.

Claim 1 refers to a general 25% tariff on vehicles imported into the US. Claim 2 specifies a negotiated reduction of duties on automobile imports from South Korea specifically to 15%, representing a distinct origin-based program.

Claim 1 cites a current 25% tariff rate as the basis for financial guidance. Claim 2 reports a future reduction to 15% announced on July 30, indicating a transition from the current rate to a new rate.

Claim 1 states the 25% tariff will apply to non-U.S. content under USMCA. Claim 2 clarifies that compliant parts remain tariff-free until a process is established to apply tariffs to that same non-U.S. content, describing the implementation mechanism.
